candidates.tagline: 8 years, 1,024 cores on paper — the chip that never shipped just went bankrupt
candidates.story: Tachyum's Prodigy processor, pitched since 2018 as a single chip beating Intel, AMD, and NVIDIA combined, missed six consecutive launch dates (2020–2025), ballooned its core-count claims from 64 to 1,024 on paper, took over $220 million in reported funding, and never publicly demonstrated working silicon before its Slovak subsidiary filed for bankruptcy on October 22, 2026.
candidates.why_funny: After eight years of raising the core count every time a launch date slipped, the only thing Tachyum actually shipped was a bankruptcy filing — Tom's Hardware had been calling it a 'meme chip' for years.
candidates.alt: News infographic reading 'TACHYUM FILES FOR BANKRUPTCY — Prodigy: 8 years, 1,024 cores on paper, no shipping chip' with a chip icon crossed out in orange and all promised launch years 2020 through 2025 struck through in red, ending with '2030+?' in an orange box

candidates.tagline: Google's AI laptop ate all its own RAM — first update frees 6GB back
candidates.story: Google's Googlebook OS, launched weeks ago as an AI-first Android laptop platform, received its first major patch on November 9, 2026 fixing 30+ bugs and recovering 3–6 GB of RAM by cutting the memory that on-device AI had been silently consuming — amounting to 20–33% of system memory on 16 GB machines.
candidates.why_funny: Google built a laptop whose headline feature was on-device AI, then the AI immediately ate a third of the laptop's memory before the user opened a single app; Thurrott called the launch state 'shoddy' and 'half-assed,' and the first update was titled '31 launch headaches.'
candidates.alt: Lenovo Googlebook 15 laptop open on a wooden coffee table, showing the Googlebook OS Android-style interface with a teal wave wallpaper and the Gemini assistant panel open on the left
